title: The Growth of Information Asymmetry Between Earnings Announcements and Its Implications for Reporting Frequency
eligible_reason: The European DiD (Tables 5-6) is not a staggered binary adoption. Firm-days are classified by reporting regime (quarterly vs semiannual firm-years, which switches in both directions as EU and UK requirements changed) and by position within the semester (treat = second half of the semester); the coefficient of interest is quarterly x treat. Every column includes time-varying controls (size, turnover, volatility, log midpoint price, first_semester) and earnings-announcement window dummies EAm5-EA5, with firm and business-day FE. The US analyses (Tables 3-4, 7) regress liquidity on days since the earnings announcement (continuous). No data are shipped.
design_notes: Scripts_to_produce_the_tables_and_figures/11_Diff_in_Diff_European_Sample__Tables_5_6.do lines 529-582 (treat, quarterly_by_treat) and 653-656 (EA_window_dummies EAm5-EA5; ctrls_dnd size turnover volatility log_adjmidpoint first_semester; absorb bizdate firm_id; cluster bizdate firm_id). 04_Main_Tests__Tables_3_4.do: reghdfe on days_since_rdq with controls.
n_eligible_specs_note: No staggered binary treatment; time-varying controls in every column.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Reporting regime switches in both directions; the DiD contrast is within-semester timing.
